newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba member-people's trust lies with central bank.
newsitem.headline: Buba member-people's trust lies with central bank.

text.p: German faith in a smooth transition from their beloved deutschemark to the euro resides more with the Bundesbank than with politicians, Bundesbank council member Ernst Welteke said in a radio interview late on Wednesday.

Welteke warned that the German parliament it should be wary of giving its majority to a government plan to override Bundesbank opposition to a revaluation of its currency reserves ahead of European monetary union.
"Politicians do not have a great deal of credit with the public at the moment," Welteke said on Deutschlandfunk radio.
"(The people's) trust that the transition period from deutschemark to euro can be a stability-oriented one lies much more with the Bundesbank than with politicians."
Currency union "had not been explained very well to the people by politicians", he added.
Welteke conceded that if the German parliament did give its approval to the plan "there was not much we (in the Bundesbank council) can do to stop it".
He said he understood a simple parliamentary majority was all the government needed to approve necessary changes in the Bundesbank statute for the plan to proceed.
